title: DOM Manipulation in Real Interfaces
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of dom manipulation in real interfaces in a jQuery application.
Apply adding and removing cart items in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify creating notification messages with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through dom manipulation in real interfaces with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns adding and removing cart items into a repeatable implementation choice. DOM manipulation changes document content. Use text setters for plain text, create elements with known attributes, and avoid inserting untrusted data as HTML.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: DOM manipulation changes document content. Use text setters for plain text, create elements with known attributes, and avoid inserting untrusted data as HTML.

content_blocks.expected_output: Creates an accessible status notice with safe text and appends it to #messages.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local HTML page with jQuery 4.0.0 loaded before app.js for JavaScript snippets. HTML and package-manager snippets can be checked as configuration examples. Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original markup and code, clear console/network filters, reload the local page, and repeat the same interaction. For a request example, return the mock endpoint to its original response before retrying.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a known DOM structure, apply the pattern for dom manipulation in real interfaces, and test one normal case plus one edge case. Keep selectors scoped to the intended component and verify the real browser result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Update a small list or message panel using dom manipulation in real interfaces. Include plain text from a variable and avoid treating untrusted values as HTML.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates dom manipulation in real interfaces using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in dom manipulation in real interfaces.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: Creates an accessible status notice with safe text and appends it to #messages.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
